title: Electrocapillarity
description: A voltage changes how well a liquid wets a surface: a drop of mercury in acid flattens or bulges as the voltage is turned up and down. Today it pushes droplets around lab chips and focuses liquid lenses.
effect: a voltage makes a drop spread out or bead up
pickWhy: The database calls it electrowetting, which took off in the 1990s; I dated it to Lippmann's 1875 discovery and renamed it to match.
edbDesc: (or Electrocapillary Effect) The modification of the wetting properties of a hydrophobic surface with an applied electric field.
